**1 — Scene:** A mixed meal of a roasted or braised bone-in shank (possibly lamb), a roasted chicken leg portion with skin, and a fresh rice-paper roll containing noodles and vegetables.

**2 — Vessel:** White dinner plate, approximately **26 cm** in diameter. Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Bone-in shank, skin-on chicken portion, and fresh rice-paper roll. No separate sauce or dressing is visible; cooking fat is included in the meat estimates.

**4 — Area:** Shank approximately **14%**, chicken **12%**, rice-paper roll **15%**. Total coverage: **41%**, consistent with the substantial exposed plate.

**5–7 — Volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Area | Average height | Gross volume | Density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Bone-in shank | 74 cm² | 2.7 cm | 200 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 190 g | 120 | 228 kcal |
| Bone-in chicken with skin | 64 cm² | 2.5 cm | 160 ml | 0.95 g/ml | 152 g | 180 | 274 kcal |
| Fresh rice-paper roll | 80 cm² | 2.7 cm | 216 ml | 0.9 g/ml | 194 g | 110 | 213 kcal |

The meat weights **include the bones**. Their energy densities are correspondingly lower than those for edible meat alone; bones contribute weight but no calories. The roll estimate includes its wrapper and visible filling.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **536 g as plated and 715 kcal** is plausible for two substantial bone-in meat portions and one large fresh roll. Edible weight would be lower after discarding bones. Meat identity, bone proportion, and hidden roll ingredients are the main uncertainties.
